content_sanskrit: इति निर्णीय दैत्येन्द्रो दामव्यालकटान्विताम् । सेनां संप्रेषयामास भूतलं देवनाशिनीम्
padaccheda: इति । निर्णीय । दैत्येन्द्रः । दामव्यालकटान्विताम् । सेनाम् । संप्रेषयामास । भूतलम् । देवनाशिनीम्
anvaya: इति निर्णीय दैत्य-इन्द्रः दाम-व्याल-कट-अन्विताम् देव-नाशिनीम् सेनाम् भू-तलम् सं-प्र-एषयामास
meaning_english: After deciding thus, the lord of the Daityas dispatched his army, led by Dāma, Vyāla, and Kaṭa, to the surface of the earth to destroy the gods.

content_sanskrit: दैत्याः सागरकुञ्जेभ्यः कन्दरेभ्यश्च सायुधाः । उदगुर्भीमनिर्ह्लादाः सपक्षगिरिलीलया
padaccheda: दैत्याः । सागरकुञ्जेभ्यः । कन्दरेभ्यः । च । सायुधाः । उदगुः । भीमनिर्ह्लादाः । सपक्षगिरिलीलया
anvaya: सा-आयुधाः भीम-निर्ह्लादाः दैत्याः स-पक्ष-गिरि-लीलया सागर-कुञ्जेभ्यः कन्दरेभ्यः च उत्-अगुः
meaning_english: Armed and uttering terrifying roars, the Daityas emerged from the ocean thickets and mountain caves with the grace of winged mountains.
Bolstered by Dāma, Vyāla, and Kaṭa, the Dānavas filled the hollow of heaven and earth, their flailing arms appearing to strike the very sun.

content_sanskrit: अथोत्तस्थुर्निकुञ्जेभ्यः कन्दरेभ्यः सुराचलात् । प्रलयान्त इवाक्षुब्धा भीमाः स्वर्वासिनां गणाः
padaccheda: अथ । उत्तस्थुः । निकुञ्जेभ्यः । कन्दरेभ्यः । सुराचलात् । प्रलयान्ते । इव । अक्षुब्धाः । भीमाः । स्वर्वासिनाम् । गणाः
anvaya: अथ सुर-अचलात् निकुञ्जेभ्यः कन्दरेभ्यः अक्षुब्धाः भीमाः स्वर्वासिनाम् गणाः प्रलय-अन्ते इव उत्-तस्थुः
meaning_english: Then, from the groves and caves of the celestial mountain Meru, the formidable and unperturbed hosts of the gods rose up as if at the end of a kalpa.

padaccheda: देवासुरपताकिन्योः । तत् । युद्धम् । अभवत् । तयोः । अकालोल्वणकल्पान्तभीषणम् । भुवनान्तरे
anvaya: तयोः देव-असुर-पताकिन्योः भुवन-अन्तरे अ-काल-उल्वण-कल्प-अन्त-भीषणम् तत् युद्धम् अभवत्
meaning_english: Between those two armies of the gods and asuras, a battle ensued within the worlds, as terrifying as an untimely and violent dissolution of the universe.

content_sanskrit: पेतुः प्रलयपर्यस्तचन्द्रार्का इव दीप्तयः । शिरांसि कुन्डलोहयोततेजःपीततमांस्यथ
padaccheda: पेतुः । प्रलयपर्यस्तचन्द्रार्काः । इव । दीप्तयः । शिरांसि । कुण्डलोद्योततेजःपीततमांसि । अथ
anvaya: अथ कुण्डल-उद्योत-तेजः-पीत-तमांसि शिरांसि प्रलय-पर्यस्त-चन्द्र-अर्काः इव दीप्तयः पेतुः
meaning_english: Then, severed heads, whose brilliance from shining earrings swallowed the darkness, fell like the sun and moon cast down during the universal dissolution.

padaccheda: जुघूर्णुः । भटनिर्मुक्तसिंहनादविराविताः । प्रलयानिलसंपूरैः । स्फुटहासाः । इव । अद्रयः
anvaya: भट-निर्मुक्त-सिंह-नाद-विराविताः (देवाः असुराः च) प्रलय-अनिल-संपूरैः स्फुट-हासाः अद्रयः इव जुघूर्णुः
meaning_english: Resounding with the lion-like roars released by the warriors, they reeled like mountains appearing to laugh loudly when struck by the winds of cosmic destruction.
The foundations of the world were shaken by strikes of weapons as heavy as mountain rocks, while fearless lions sought refuge on the slopes of the principal mountain ranges.

padaccheda: चेरुः । परस्पराघातहतहेतिसमुत्थिताः । लोलानलकणाः । कल्पविशीर्णाः । इव । तारकाः
anvaya: परस्पर-आघात-हत-हेति-समुत्थिताः लोलाः अनल-कणाः कल्प-विशीर्णाः तारकाः इव चेरुः
meaning_english: Flickering sparks of fire, rising from weapons clashing against each other, moved about like stars scattered at the end of an eon.

padaccheda: विलेसुः । रक्तमांसौघपूर्णैकार्णवतीरगाः । कल्पतालवत् । उत्तालाः । वेतालाः । तालतालिताः
anvaya: रक्त-मांस-ओघ-पूर्ण-एक-अर्णव-तीर-गाः कल्प-तालवत् उत्तालाः ताल-तालिताः वेतालाः विलेसुः
meaning_english: Moving along the shores of a single ocean filled with floods of blood and flesh, formidable Vetālas, as tall as the palmyra trees at the end of time, reveled while clapping their hands.
In the sky, where the rising dust had been settled by the pouring showers of throbbing blood, there appeared millions of crowns and earrings shattered by the blows of weapons.

padaccheda: बभूवुः । भास्कराकारैः । कल्पभूरुहधारिभिः । प्रहारदलिताद्रीन्द्रैः । दैत्यैः । निर्विवराः । दिशः
anvaya: भास्कर-आकारैः कल्प-भूरुह-धारिभिः प्रहार-दलित-अद्रि-इन्द्रैः दैत्यैः दिशः निर्विवराः बभूवुः ।
meaning_english: The quarters of the sky became completely filled, without any gaps, by the Daityas who possessed sun-like brilliance, carried celestial Kalpavṛkṣa trees, and had shattered great mountains with their strikes.

padaccheda: जग्मुः । ज्वलदसिप्रान्तवातपातितभित्तयः । कणप्रकरताम् । शैलाः । कल्पाग्निदलिताः । इव
anvaya: ज्वलत्-असि-प्रान्त-वात-पातित-भित्तयः शैलाः कल्प-अग्नि-दलिताः इव कण-प्रकरतां जग्मुः ।
meaning_english: The mountains, whose ridges were brought down by the wind generated from the edges of flaming swords, were reduced to a heap of particles, as if shattered by the fire of cosmic dissolution.

content_sanskrit: देवास्ते च समाजग्मुरश्वमेधैधिता इव । असुरानस्त्रविभ्रष्टाञ्जलदानिव वायवः
padaccheda: देवाः । ते । च । समाजग्मुः । अश्वमेधैधिताः । असुरान् । अस्त्रविभ्रष्टान् । जलदान् । इव । वायवः
anvaya: अश्वमेध-एधिताः देवाः ते च अस्त्र-विभ्रष्टान् असुरान् वायवः जलदान् इव समाजग्मुः ।
meaning_english: The gods, invigorated by Aśvamedha sacrifices, fell upon the Asuras—who were already reeling from the weapons—just as powerful winds scatter the clouds.

padaccheda: जगृहुः । तान् । अथ । आक्रम्य । जरठासून् । इव । औतवः । ते । अपि । तान् । जगृहुः । मत्तान् । ऋक्षारूढान् । इव । द्रुमान्
anvaya: अथ औतवः जरठ-आसून् इव तान् आक्रम्य जगृहुः ते अपि ऋक्ष-आरूढान् द्रुमान् इव मत्तान् तान् जगृहुः ।
meaning_english: Then, the gods seized the Asuras like cats pouncing on old mice; the Asuras in turn grabbed the intoxicated gods, like trees being seized by climbing bears.

content_sanskrit: दोर्वृक्षविलसद्धेतिकुसुमाः शस्त्रपल्लवाः । रेजुः सुरासुराः फुल्ला वनलोला इव द्रुमाः
padaccheda: दोर्वृक्षविलसद्धेतिकुसुमाः । शस्त्रपल्लवाः । रेजुः । सुरासुराः । फुल्लाः । वनलोलाः । इव । द्रुमाः
anvaya: दोः-वृक्ष-विलसत्-हेति-कुसुमाः शस्त्र-पल्लवाः सुरासुराः वन-लोलाः फुल्लाः द्रुमाः इव रेजुः ।
meaning_english: With their tree-like arms bearing weapons as flowers and missiles as tender leaves, the Devas and Asuras shone like blossoming trees swaying in a forest.

content_sanskrit: अन्योन्यं पूरयामासुः शस्त्रपूरैर्दिशो दश । वनानि कुसुमव्रातैः सुमेराविव मारुतः
padaccheda: अन्योन्यम् । पूरयामासुः । शस्त्रपूरैः । दिशः । दश । वनानि । कुसुमव्रातैः । सुमेरौ । इव । मारुतः
anvaya: सुमेरौ मारुतः कुसुम-व्रातैः वनानि इव (ते) शस्त्र-पूरैः अन्योन्यं दश दिशः पूरयामासुः ।
meaning_english: Just as the wind fills the forests of Mount Sumeru with heaps of flowers, they filled the ten directions by showering weapons upon one another.

anvaya: रोदः-रन्ध्र-उदुम्बर-अन्तः महा-मशक-संघयोः देव-दानव-सेनयोः घोरं युद्धं समभवत् ।
meaning_english: A terrible battle took place between the armies of the gods and the demons, who appeared like swarms of large gnats fighting inside the hollow of a giant Udumbara fruit formed by the space between heaven and earth.

padaccheda: अथ । उदपतत् । उत्तालैः । लोकपालेभमण्डलैः । कल्पाभ्रस्फूर्जिताकारः । दारुणः । समरारवः
anvaya: अथ उत्तालैः लोकपाल-इभ-मण्डलैः कल्प-अभ्र-स्फूर्जित-आकारः दारुणः समर-आरवः उदपतत् ।
meaning_english: Then, a dreadful roar of battle arose, resembling the thundering of clouds at the end of an aeon, intensified by the trumpeting of the circles of elephants belonging to the Lokapālas.

content_sanskrit: पिण्डग्रहेण नभसि भूभागमिव कुट्टिमम् । मुष्टिग्राह्यो महामेघमन्थरोदरपीवरः
padaccheda: पिण्डग्रहेण । नभसि । भूभागम् । इव । कुट्टिमम् । मुष्टिग्राह्यः । महामेघमन्थरोदरपीवरः
anvaya: नभसि पिण्ड-ग्रहेण भू-भागम् इव कुट्टिमम् मुष्टि-ग्राह्यः महा-मेघ-मन्थर-उदर-पीवरः (धूलिः उदतिष्ठत्) ।
meaning_english: A thick dust arose in the sky, appearing solid enough to be grasped by the hand and as dense as the interior of a great slow-moving cloud, making the firmament look like a paved floor.

The battle resembled a theater of crying actors where mountains of weapons were crushed by the collision of chariots, and it echoed with the gurgling, harsh screams of those whose hearts were failing as their life-force ebbed away.

The roar of the battle increased like the tumultuous sound of the world's end during pralaya, appearing like the golden mountain Meru melting under the intense heat of the simultaneous rising of the twelve suns.

content_sanskrit: ब्रह्माण्डकुण्डसंघट्टात्परावृत्त्या च निर्गतः । महास्रोतःपयःपूरः सत्त्वाहत इवाकरः
padaccheda: ब्रह्माण्ड-कुण्ड-संघट्टात् । परावृत्त्या । च । निर्गतः । महा-स्रोतः-पयः-पूरः । सत्त्व-आहतः । इव । आकरः
anvaya: (सः रणः) ब्रह्माण्ड-कुण्ड-संघट्टात् परावृत्त्या निर्गतः सत्त्व-आहतः आकरः महा-स्रोतः-पयः-पूरः इव (आसीत्) ।
meaning_english: Like a massive flood of water bursting forth after striking the rim of the cosmic egg, the battle surged like an ocean disturbed by powerful sea monsters.
The noise of the battle moved like the sound of the flapping wings of the great ancient winged mountains, and its intense pressure caused the caves of the mighty peaks to shatter and burst.
With its form resembling the churning of the Milky Ocean by Mount Mandara, the battle's booming explosions and deep vibrations shook the islands, the creatures, and the very earth.

padaccheda: सेनयोः । क्षुब्धयोः । आसीत् । युद्धम् । उद्धत-दानवम् । निष्पिष्ट-नगर-ग्राम-गिरि-कानन-मानवम्
anvaya: क्षुब्धयोः सेनयोः उद्धत-दानवम् (तथा) निष्पिष्ट-नगर-ग्राम-गिरि-कानन-मानवम् युद्धम् आसीत् ।
meaning_english: Between the two agitated armies, a fierce battle involving arrogant Dānavas broke out, crushing cities, villages, mountains, forests, and men alike.
The quarters of the sky were filled with mountain-like Dānavas severed by hundreds of great weapons, while the belly of the heavens was choked with the dust of weapons clashing against one another.
The impact of the circling bhuśuṇḍī weapons shattered hundreds of peaks of Mount Meru, while the gale-force winds of arrows mowed down the lotus-like faces of both Daityas and gods.
Gods and Daityas were whirled around like withered straw in hundreds of circular weapon-eddies, as the sky was enveloped by the surging waves of the armies' strikes.

Crowds of celestial beings fell as their chariots were crushed by the fierce winds of weapons, and the cities of the sky were submerged by the floods of water rising from oceans conjured by divine missiles.
The battle flowed with hundreds of rivers formed by the falling of great weapons, swords, tridents, and spears; the pavilion of the universe shook from the fierce impact of mountain-like wings.
The city of Brahmā fell under the mass of blows from the heels of demons, while the palaces rang with the sound of jingling bangles amidst the tumultuous cries of women.
The battlefield was filled with waters from the streams of intoxicating blood arising from the fallen demon forces, where men washed in gore fled amidst fierce, liberated cries.

The battlefield was filled with Yama appearing and disappearing, covered by the lotus-like guardians of the worlds, and it was chaotic with the sight of armies shattered by the blows of gods and demons.
Terrifying with a great buzzing sound and the noise of 'shava-shava' emanating from floating corpses, the battle surged with the movements of mountain-sized demons resembling winged peaks.
The entire earth, oceans, and mountains were reddened by the blood flowing like torrents from the mountain-like demons pierced by the tips of weapons.
Nations, cities, forests, villages, and caves were destroyed, while mountains were formed by the piled corpses of countless demons, elephants, horses, and men.
The battle shone with elephants struck by rows of long, swift iron arrows, and the intoxicated elephant Airāvaṇa had its shoulders crushed by the blows of fists.
Mountains were shattered by torrential rains from the clouds of the Kalpa dissolution, and the great ancestral peaks were crushed and sent flying by the impact of mighty thunderbolts.
Demons were incinerated by the nets of flames from the wrathful fire, while that very fire was extinguished by the oceans brought forth in the hollow of a single palm.
The battle raged with intense flames solidified by the massive array of fierce demons, where the tongues of fire, fueled by forest-like formations, melted the watery mountain peaks.
The conflict resembled the night of cosmic dissolution with irresistible darkness created by missiles, yet the thick veil of darkness was swallowed by the radiance of a multitude of illusory suns.
The torrential rain from dark clouds was sucked dry by showers of illusory fire, while the clashing of weapons produced hissing flames and a downpour of sparks.

The chaos of mountain-hurling missiles was quelled by thunderbolt-showering weapons; the battle was rich with the duel of sleep-inducing and awakening missiles, characterized by a deadlock of conflicting forces.

anvaya: (तत् युद्धं) वहत्-क्रकच-वृक्ष-अस्त्रम् (आसीत्), जल-अग्नि-अस्मरण-अन्धितम् (आसीत्), ब्रह्म-अस्त्र-युद्ध-विषमम् (तथा च) तमः-तेजः-अस्त्र-सारितम् (आसीत्) ।
meaning_english: Wielding saw-like tree missiles, the combatants were blinded by the mutual cancellation of water and fire weapons; the struggle became precarious due to Brahmāstra duels and the shifting dominance of light and dark missiles.
The entire sky was rendered seamless by the armies of weapons vomited forth by missiles, being crushed by showers of stones and illuminated by the blaze of fire-showering weapons.

anvaya: (तत् युद्धं) पताका-स्पृष्ट-शशिकैः चक्र-चीत्कार-गर्जितैः रथैः मुहूर्तेन लङ्घित-उदय-अस्तमय-अचलम् (आसीत्) ।
meaning_english: With chariots whose banners brushed the moon and whose wheels creaked with thunderous roars, the mountains of sunrise and sunset were traversed in a mere moment.
In that battle, great demons were incessantly dying from the strikes of thunderbolts, yet they were being brought back to life by the great science of Śukra and the immortals.

anvaya: (तस्मिन् युद्धे) विद्रवद्-देव-संघातम् (आसीत्), जय-प्रोद्-डामर-अमरम् (आसीत्), शुभ-ग्रह-महा-केतु-मालिकानाम् इतः ततः (गमनम् आसीत्) ।
meaning_english: Groups of gods fled in retreat while others triumphed fiercely; meanwhile, garlands of auspicious planets and great comets were tossed hither and thither.
The spectacle made the neck of the intellect crane to observe the flood of portents and auspicious signs, as the entire world—mountains, sky, earth, oceans, and heavens—turned into an ocean of blood.

anvaya: (तत् युद्धम्) दुर्वार-वैरतः फुल्ल-एक-किंशुक-वनं कुर्वत् (तथा च) पर्वत-प्रतिमा-असंख्य-शव-पूर्ण-महा-अर्णवम् (इव अभवत्) ।
meaning_english: Due to irresistible enmity, the battlefield resembled a forest of blossoming Kiṃśuka trees and became a vast ocean filled with countless corpses as large as mountains.

anvaya: समग्र-तरु-शाखा-अग्र-लम्ब-लोल-महा-शवम् दीप्यमानैः स्व-वात-आर्तैः पक्ष-पुष्पैः लसत्-फलैः (च युक्तम् अभवत्) ।
meaning_english: Great corpses hung and swayed from the tips of all tree branches, while the wings of birds, appearing like flowers and fruits, shone as they were tossed by the winds.

anvaya: ताल-उत्तालैः शर-व्रात-वनैः व्याप्त-नभः-स्थलम् पर्वत-प्रतिमा-संख्य-कबन्धा-शत-बाहुभिः (च युक्तम् अभवत्) ।
meaning_english: The sky was pervaded by forests of arrows as tall as palms, and by the hundreds of arms of headless trunks that were as massive as mountains.
The dancing trunks caused clouds, celestial chariots, gods, and stars to fall, while mountains were pierced by arrows, spears, clubs, darts, and sharp-edged missiles.
The sky was strewn with fragments of walls fallen from the seven worlds, echoing with the continuous, deep thundering of intoxicated clouds of Pralaya like firm drums.
Thus, the elephants of the netherworld roared at the hundreds of sounds, and tall Daitya-mountains were dragged by the trunk of Vināyaka.
The hosts of Siddhas, Sādhyas, and Maruts stood motionless in one direction, while Gandharvas, Kinnaras, gods, and Cāraṇas fled in terror.

content_sanskrit: वघुरशनिनिपातखण्डिताङ्गा दलितशिलाशकलाः ककुम्मुखेषु । प्रलयसमयसूचकाः सुराणां सुरतरुघर्घरघस्मराः समीराः
padaccheda: ववृधुः । अशनिनिपातखण्डिताङ्गाः । दलितशिलाशकलाः । ककुम्मुखेषु । प्रलयसमयसूचकाः । सुराणाम् । सुरतरुघर्घरघस्मराः । समीराः
anvaya: ववृधुः अशनि-निपात-खण्डित-अङ्गाः दलित-शिला-शकलाः ककुप्-मुखेषु प्रलय-समय-सूचकाः सुराणाम् सुर-तरु-घर्घर-घस्मराः समीराः ।
meaning_english: Winds grew violent in all directions, shattering limbs like thunderbolts and crushing stones into fragments; signaling the time of dissolution, these winds greedily devoured the celestial trees with a gurgling roar.
